title: Flockdeck stream recording line, format version 1
description: One line of a Flockdeck stream recording (JSON Lines): the JSON-RPC traffic between Flockdeck and a structured agent. This file is the definition of the format: a line is valid if it validates here, and a line with a field not named for its type is not one Flockdeck writes. No field is ever null. docs/rpc-recording-format.md explains the rest.

seq.description: Line number within the file, from 1. It rises on every line and never repeats. It has gaps only after a rpc_dropped line, whose own seq is that of the last line dropped.

time.description: When the message was seen by Flockdeck, RFC 3339, UTC. For a coalesced message, when the first of them was.

session.description: The recording's id: its file name without .jsonl.

dir.description: in: the agent sent it. out: Flockdeck sent it. On rpc_message lines only.

msg.description: The JSON-RPC message as it was, after redaction and clipping, and for a coalesced message the merged one. Numbers keep their exact digits.

raw.description: A line of traffic that was not a JSON object, redacted and cut at 8 KiB.

text.description: A sentence saying what a rpc_started, rpc_dropped or rpc_stopped line is, or what became of a message that was too long to keep.

until.description: When the last of a coalesced message's parts was seen. Present only when merged is.

merged.description: How many messages a coalesced line stands for. Absent for a message that stands alone.

project.description: The project's name. On rpc_started only.

agent.description: The agent's id. On rpc_started only.

conversation.description: The conversation id Flockdeck had for the pane, cut at 256 bytes. On rpc_started only, and absent when there was none.

dropped.description: How many lines were dropped from the start of the file so far, to keep it within its size cap. On rpc_dropped only.

redacted.description: Present, and true, when redaction replaced something in the line.

clipped.description: How many strings in the line were cut, or 1 for a message that was not kept because it was too long.
